tagline: Robert Moses's parkways out across the bays to the beaches.
intro: Of the six parkways, the Wantagh and the Meadowbrook cross the bays to the barrier islands, and the short Loop hops from Point Lookout to meet the Meadowbrook. The Bay and Ocean parkways run side by side through Jones Beach State Park, and the Ocean goes on to Captree. The Bethpage runs north through the Massapequa Preserve to Bethpage State Park.

When Robert Moses's surveyors first saw Jones Island in the 1920s it stood two feet above the sea. Dredges pumped sand from the bay bottom until it stood twelve, and in 1928 thousands of men planted beach grass by hand to hold it. The beach and its causeway, the first piece of the Wantagh, opened on August 4, 1929.

moments.title: Jones Beach State Park
moments.text: Where the Wantagh meets the Ocean Parkway, the road circles an Italianate water tower that Moses set there as the park's centerpiece, known locally as the Pencil.

moments.title: Gilgo
moments.text: The parkway runs past beach houses on land leased from the state, some of them at West Gilgo floated over by barge from High Hill Beach to make room for Jones Beach.

moments.title: Oak Beach
moments.text: Inhabited since a lifesaving station stood here out of reach overland, the community stayed mostly summer cottages until the Robert Moses Causeway arrived in 1951.

sources.label: NYSDOT, Historic Long Island Scenic Parkways
